newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ uncertainty won't much alter outlook - Treasury.
newsitem.headline: NZ uncertainty won't much alter outlook - Treasury.

text.p: Any uncertainty generated by the government formation process in New Zealand was not expected to have a substantial impact on the economy, Treasury said in its December Economic and Fiscal Update published on Monday.
Treasury said its overall growth forecasts were very similar to those contained in the Pre-Election Economic and Fiscal Update, but the composition of growth had changed.
"The TWI is expected to average 67.0 in the December quarter -- the PreFU forecast was 65.3.
"A higher exchange rate means that net exports are lower than in the PreFU," Treasury said.
"On the other hand, long term interest rates are currently lower than expected, and this is expected to sustain overall growth at around the level expected in the PreFU."

A sharp rebound in business confidence in the September quarter had reduced the likelihood of a sinificant slowdown in business development. "As a consequence, we have revised up business investment growth in 1996/97," Treasury said.

The outlook for wages was slightly stronger than in the PreFU, owing to a high private sector wage outturn for the year to August, and the prospect of stronger wage growth in the public sector over the next year.
"Inflation in the last few years of the forecasts is now expected to be slightly higher than in the PreFU," Treasury said.
